unit.title: Pluperfect (pluscuamperfecto)
unit.subtitle: había + participle: the past before the past

grammar.title: The action that happened even earlier
grammar.intro: The pluperfect (pluscuamperfecto) is your “had done” tense. It marks an action that was already finished before another past moment. Build it with the imperfect of haber (había…) plus a participle. When you say “When I arrived, they had already eaten,” the eating came first — that earlier action is the pluperfect.

sections.heading: había + participle
sections.body: Take the imperfect of haber and add the participle (-ar → -ado, -er/-ir → -ido). The participle never changes for person or gender here:

ex.en: I had already spoken with him.

sections.heading: Irregular participles
sections.body: A few common participles are irregular — memorise these, you'll reuse them everywhere:

ex.en: I had never seen the sea.

sections.heading: Two past actions in order
sections.body: Use the pluperfect for the earlier action and the preterite for the later one. Words like ya (already) and todavía no (not yet) love this tense:

ex.en: When I arrived, I had already eaten.
I hadn't finished yet when it rang.

takeaways: It marks an action finished before another past moment.
Irregular participles: hecho, visto, dicho, escrito, vuelto.
Pair it with the preterite: Cuando llegué, ya había comido.

mistakes.why: The earlier action needs the pluperfect (había comido), not the preterite comí.
After haber you need the participle (comido), not the infinitive.
The participle of ver is irregular: visto, not 'ver'.

exercises.prompt_en: When I arrived, they had already eaten.
exercises.no: The earlier past action uses the pluperfect: “habían comido”.

exercises.prompt: Nunca ___ el mar antes de ese día.
exercises.prompt_en: I had never seen the sea before that day.
exercises.no: Use haber + the participle visto: “había visto”.

exercises.prompt: Build: “When I arrived, I had already eaten.”
exercises.no: “Cuando llegué, ya había comido” — the earlier action uses the pluperfect.

exercises.prompt_en: I hadn't finished yet when you called.
exercises.no: The pluperfect uses the imperfect of haber: “había”.

exercises.scenario: A friend offers you dinner, but you're late 🍽️

lines.speaker: Marta
lines.en: Do you want to have dinner with us?

options.text: Gracias, pero ya había comido antes de venir.
Gracias, pero ya como antes de venir.
Gracias, pero ya comeré antes de venir.

exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! Acción anterior al presente pasado → había comido.
exercises.no: The eating happened before you arrived, so use the pluperfect: “ya había comido antes de venir”.
